time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame 0 at t = 0; last frame 71 at t = 2.958 s
units: pixels (x right, y down, origin top-left of the 2560x1440 frame) and seconds; no metric scale assumed

camera.evidence: phase correlation of the top 300 rows vs frame 0: |shift| <= 0.16 px in all frames (tracks/camera_shift.csv). Large mean abs diff (~50 grey levels) is the animated water caustics + render noise, not camera motion.
camera.view: elevated oblique view looking down at a flat sea floor (sand with animated caustic light pattern); whale swims above the floor
camera.horizon: not visible; the floor fills the whole frame. Very top-right corner (x>2400, y<30) is slightly darker (distant floor/fog). Caustic texture compresses toward the top of the image => floor recedes upward (farther = higher in image).
camera.focal_length: unknown (estimate from given depth_info + a known size)

objects.name: whale
objects.description: large blue humpback-type whale, the only moving object; deep blue back, dark navy underside, pale/white undersides of fluke and pectoral fins; long left pectoral fin hangs down-left; a second (right) pectoral fin becomes visible under the body from ~frame 40
objects.partly_cut_frames: 8-39: tail/fluke extends below the bottom image edge (y=1439)

reference_point_proxies.head_top: topmost mask pixel (top of head); smooth, nearly linear path (1180,390) at f0 -> (1000,298) at f71; best proxy for the body/root translation because it is not affected by tail beats
reference_point_proxies.mask_centroid: cx_px, cy_px: centroid of the colour mask; strongly influenced by tail motion and by the missed pale fluke, so it is NOT a clean origin

pixel_sizes.note: whale is seen obliquely (foreshortened) and bends its tail; pixel length varies with pose

manual_fluke_tip_px._note: read by eye on 50-px grid crops (scripts/tailcrops.py), +-8 px; the colour mask misses the pale fluke in late frames

objects.name: whale_shadow
objects.description: dark grey-brown whale-shaped cast shadow on the sea floor, below and to the lower right of the whale (light from upper left)
objects.visible_frames: 0-71; its tail runs off the bottom edge in frames 0-66
objects.note: the shadow is on the floor plane; its offset from the whale relates to whale height above floor and sun direction. Pectoral-fin part of the shadow was partly missed in frames 9-33.

objects.name: sea_floor
objects.description: flat sandy floor covering the whole image with an animated bright caustic pattern

objects.name: seabed_props
objects.description: small cluster of seabed decorations directly beneath the whale, only revealed as the whale rises/rolls (mostly hidden by the whale before ~frame 50); positions at frame 71

tall_seaweed_strand_right.note: top hidden behind whale fin/body, height is a lower bound

events.event: whale already swimming; head moving steadily up-left in image (away from camera / forward) during the whole clip
tail fluke reaches bottom image edge (cut until frame 39); tail beating downward
fluke re-enters frame; tail sweeps upward from here (fluke tip y 1130 -> 381 by frame 71)
approx: whale starts rolling, pale belly/fluke underside and right pectoral fin become visible; seabed props uncovered
end of clip, tail raised nearly horizontal to the right

apparent_size_trend: head-top track moves ~205 px up-left over the clip (smooth) -> whale moving slightly farther from camera; mask area falls 385k -> 213k px but mostly due to tail pose/roll and missed pale parts, not depth

files.tracks/whale.csv: per-frame whale mask measures + head_top and far point
